03/14.06.2024
Both these anticipatory bail applications arise out of the same police case.
Accordingly, they are being tagged together and disposed of by a common order.

Heard the parties Petitioners are apprehending their arrest in connection with Jamtara Cyber Crime P.S. Case No. 14 of 2024, for the offences registered under Sections 414, 419, 420, 467, 468,471 and 120(B) of the Indian Penal Code and under Sections 66(B)(C)(D) of the I.T. Act, pending in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge-1st, Jamtara.
On 02.03.2024 at about 11:15 A.M., Cyber police Jamtara, on the basis of confidential information,
raided the house of one Umesh Yadav and apprehended petitioners and other co-accused persons.

accused persons in their confession have named these petitioners that they were also present at the place of occurrence and some managed to escape on seeing the police party.
It was submitted that petitioners have got no criminal antecedent.
This fact has been mentioned at page 9, paragraph 13 in the anticipatory bail application.
Considering the aforesaid facts, I am inclined to extend the privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioners.

Accordingly, the petitioners, above named, are directed to surrender before the learned court below within two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and the learned court below on their surrender, shall release them on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 25,000/-
(Rupees Twenty five Thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge- 1st, Jamtara
in connection with Jamtara Cyber Crime P.S. Case No. 14 of 2024, subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
